items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1995-07-21
items.q: Buddy Johnson played down there. Favorite piano player of mine.

ctx.x: Was that about why you bought the Zoot Suit?

Well, yes, because it was a style at the time. John McNeely, Charles Dimes, myself, Edward Johnson, we were all good friends. And we all would meet down on Rampart Street and we'd party at the Pelican or sometime we went to the Tick Tock. We used to go to the, see, then we'd go to the Palace Theater where all the big bands would come. And we had Savannah Churchill, where Red Fox, where, let's see who all would come down there. I'm just trying to think of one of them. Buddy Johnson played down there. Favorite…
So, what was, when you talked about Rampart Street, was that like the happening?

items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1996-08-23
items.q: We had bands coming down to New Orleans like in 45 and 46. Buddy Johnson came down here, and he brought a new kind of singer.

ctx.x: Because this was what you would call spiritual rejuvenation. A lot of people didn't understand what was happening with the blues, especially some of the white bands who just started picking up on the blues into the late 80s, that the blues really came out of the black church. And, well, prior to that, the sacrifices that blacks made were harmed from the soul because they paid so many dues. And then, as I talked with my old great uncles from way back when they spoke with their ancestors and relatives during the…
Did that cause the demise of that club? Because I don't think it...
